_: THE PRICE LIST. Every number a customer pays lives in this file and nowhere else.
Not in a constant, not in a values file, not in a service. A price in code is a price that
needs a deploy to change, and a price that needs a deploy is one nobody changes — so the real
price list becomes a spreadsheet somebody keeps beside it, and the two disagree within a month.
ci/check_no_prices.py fails the build if a price appears in any Python we wrote.
AMOUNTS ARE IN HALALAS and include VAT, because that is what a Saudi customer is quoted: the
shop owner sees 148 and pays 148. amount 14800 is 148.00 SAR.
A BASE AND APPS, NOT FOUR TIERS
A ladder sells the wrong thing. A workshop that wants campaigns and will never look at an
association engine had to buy the engine to reach them, and read the difference between four
columns to find that out. Worse for us: every new thing we build has to be slotted into a
tier, which reprices three plans and re-argues the whole page. Invoicing and CRM are coming,
and the ladder has no room for them that does not disturb what is already sold.
So: ONE base that is the product working, and each app bought on its own. He pays for what he
turned on, the page is a shop rather than a comparison table, and a new app is a row here.
HOW IT ADDS UP, AND WHY IT NEEDS NO NEW CODE. billing-service resolves entitlements across
EVERY live subscription and merges them — its own words: 'per-item catalogue — one
subscription per product — the union IS the entitlement'. Rich limits merge by combining
`limit`, and numbers SUM: the base says feature.campaigns 0, the app says 1, the answer is 1.
Seats add the same way — base 5 plus a seat pack of 10 is 15.
WHICH IS WHY ONLY THE BASE MAY CARRY `messages.monthly`, AND WHY ITS VALUE IS THE WORD
`unlimited` RATHER THAN -1. billing merges its own sentinel by beating every arithmetic;
-1 is just a number to it, and two of them summed to -2 — which refuses every send.
The one-row rule holds for any key carrying the sentinel: it belongs to exactly one row.
AND AN APP IS NOT BOUGHT TWICE, NOR WITHOUT THE BASE. Neither is expressible in billing —
subscribe always creates a row — so both are refused in our own path, operations'
`subscription.activate`, which is the only door the console uses. It decides from the
SUBSCRIPTIONS THEMSELVES (/internal/billing/subscriptions, base-services v0.16.7): a row is a
BASE when it carries `messages.monthly`, which is the one key an app may never repeat. An
earlier `feature.base` flag said the same thing less well — it could not name WHICH
subscription, WHEN it renews or WHAT was paid — and it is gone.
LIMITS ARE THE PRODUCT. The name sells; the limits dict is what actually happens. Three kinds,
and the difference decides who reports the number:
counter  consumed by whoever spends it, reset per period  — messages, custom templates
gauge    the CURRENT value of something owned elsewhere    — seats, branches
boolean  on or off                                          — the apps
AND 0 IS NOT ABSENCE. `0` means the key exists and the answer is DENY — which the console can
render as «هذا تطبيق لم تشترِه بعد، وهذا زر شرائه». A key missing everywhere means NOT
ENTITLED with no reason to show. So THE BASE CARRIES EVERY KEY, including the zeros, and every
shop therefore has an answer for every key whatever else it bought.
AND WE DO NOT SELL MESSAGES. The establishment contracts with Meta directly and Meta bills it
per delivered message, on a card in its own account — we neither buy them nor resell them, so
selling '1,000 a month' was selling what we do not own. Top-up packs went with it.
messages.monthly SURVIVES AS THE SENTINEL, and that is the whole point: unlimited still
counter in billing, so every send is measured and nothing is ever refused for a ceiling of
ours. It is a protection meter — it catches our own runaway loop before the owner's bill does
— and if we ever become a Solution Partner and messages are billed to us, a real number goes
back in this one field and the packs return unchanged.
His actual limit is what WhatsApp allows: 250 unique customers a day before verification,
2,000 after (spec 6.2.2). A second ceiling from us on top of theirs is a number he explains
twice and understands once.

limit_keys.messages.monthly: measured, never sold — see the note above. Uncapped, on the BASE ONLY
limit_keys.staff.seats: people who can sign in; operations owns the count and reports it
limit_keys.branches: branches; operations owns the count and reports it
limit_keys.feature.insights.engine: the association engine (§10.6) — the one thing nobody else has
limit_keys.feature.api: the programmatic link: a till writing visits in the shop's name
limit_keys.templates.custom: templates he writes himself and submits to Meta, per month
limit_keys.feature.base: the base itself — the visit register. Enforced on every write in operations and reminders (core/base_licence.py); a lapsed month keeps reading and stops writing
limit_keys.feature.bookings: the appointment scheduler (docs/وصف-تطبيق-الحجوزات.md) — the staff-side grid, drag-and-drop reschedule, and the booking-to-visit gateway
limit_keys.feature.rating: the post-visit rating app (WhatsApp Flow, stars + free text) — replaces the plain visit-confirmation message for a shop that owns it, never a second message
limit_keys.feature.whatsapp: the AI assistant over WhatsApp — an AI-composed reply and AI-driven booking for this shop's customers. THE ONE APP THAT MAY BE BOUGHT STANDALONE, WITHOUT الأساس first (see its own plan row's `plan.standalone` — services/operations/app/core/subscribe.py::may_add reads it)
limit_keys.feature.contacts: جهات الاتصال — a FREE standalone app that does one thing: it lets a shop with no other product at all resolve-or-create a customer by phone (POST /field/customers/ensure, services/operations). Carries `plan.standalone` for the same reason `feature.whatsapp` does — a shop buying only this holds no base underneath it
limit_keys.feature.visit: تسجيل زيارة — the visit register itself, pulled out from under `feature.base`'s exclusive control and sold as its own standalone app. A shop holding EITHER `feature.base` OR this may record a visit (services/operations/app/api/subscribed.py::subscribed_write_or_visit); `feature.base` keeps its old meaning unchanged for existing subscribers — retiring it in favour of this key everywhere is a separate, future migration decision, not this one

_removed: feature.roles.custom IS GONE, and its absence is the honest state. It was sold on every tier
and the product has three fixed roles with no screen that creates a fourth — a line on an
invoice for something that does not exist. `ci/check_entitlements.py` found it the moment the
guard stopped counting a price-list LABEL as enforcement. It comes back the day it is built,
as its own app row, and nobody was charged for it in the meantime.

_: THE BASE — the product working. Visits, customers, the service catalogue, visit
confirmation and the reminder that brings people back, the customer's own page, and the
free indicators in «محلّي».
IT CARRIES EVERY KEY, including every app at 0, so no surface anywhere has to tell 'not
bought' apart from 'never heard of it'.
THE TRIAL LIVES HERE, and now it can only live here — there is no higher tier to hand him
for two weeks and take away. He evaluates the product itself; the apps are bought when a
number in his own dashboard makes him want one.
0 MEANS NO TRIAL, and the length is set from our panel by editing this row. No service
knows the number, and a shop that signed up under 14 days keeps 14 whatever we change.
RETIRED FROM NEW SIGNUPS — `listed: false`, the owner's own decision, once there was no
real subscriber anywhere to migrate (test server, never launched). The bundle this row
sold is now two separately-priced standalone apps — «جهات الاتصال» (free, granted to
every fresh shop on day one regardless, signup.py::_start_contacts_grant) and «تسجيل
زيارة» (the visit register itself, sold on its own). `base_plan_id()` deliberately reads
without `include_hidden`, so a fresh signup now finds none and skips the base-trial step
cleanly — no crash, no empty-string plan_id passed anywhere; see that function's own
note. This row is NOT retired (`active` stays true) — it is not deleted or deactivated,
only removed from the storefront, because deleting the row itself would be pointless
surgery on a plan nobody outside this file has ever held.
plans.name: الأساس

_: THE APPS. Each grants ONE key and says nothing about anything else — a row that repeated
`staff.seats` would add its number to the base's every time somebody bought it.
ONE PRICE FOR EVERY APP — 99. The first cut derived four different prices from the old
ladder, and the ladder is exactly what we stopped selling: a shop comparing 60 against
200 is reading a tier list again, and asking us to justify why one app costs three of
another.
One number ends that conversation. He reads the sentence about what an app DOES and says
yes or no — which is the decision we want him making, and the only one he can make fast.
AND IT IS EASIER TO SELL THAN TO PRICE. «كل تطبيق بـ99» is repeatable by a partner on a
phone call; four numbers are a page somebody has to open.
plans.name: الحملات

_: REQUIRES_ANY (2026-09-09), THE OWNER'S OWN REASONING: points earned on nothing are not a
programme, they are a promise with no way to keep it. Loyalty points are earned by a
customer TOUCHPOINT — a visit recorded, or an appointment attended — and a shop holding
NEITHER تسجيل زيارة nor الحجوزات (and not الأساس, which carries the same visit register)
has no way for a single point to ever be earned. `plan.requires_any` says so, data-driven,
exactly like `plan.standalone` above: `may_add` (services/operations/app/core/
subscribe.py) refuses the purchase unless the shop's own held entitlements already
intersect this list — independent of, and in addition to, the ordinary base-required
rule. A THIRD app may declare its own dependency the same way, with one edit here and
zero code changes.
plans.name: برنامج النقاط

plans.name: التقييم

_: THE ONE APP SOLD WITHOUT الأساس UNDERNEATH IT — a shop with no other product at all can buy
just this and connect its own WhatsApp number. `plan.standalone` is the marker
`services/operations/app/core/subscribe.py::may_add` reads to skip its own base-required
rule for THIS plan only — every other app row still needs الأساس first, unchanged. Shaped
as an ordinary boolean limit (not under the `feature.` prefix, so it grants nothing and
`ci/check_entitlements.py` never treats it as a sold capability) so billing merges it the
same well-tested way it merges every other boolean flag.
199, THE OWNER'S OWN PRICE (2026-09-06) — high enough to bundle a real included usage
allowance with it rather than selling bare access; see the `credits` note below.
NAMED FOR WHAT IT DOES, NOT FOR THE CHANNEL — the owner's own decision: the plan's NAME
never says WhatsApp, and DOES say 'bot'/'smart' (an AI capability is the whole sell). The
channel is named honestly in the one place a buyer needs it spelled out —
LIMIT_WORDS['feature.whatsapp'] on the pricing page (apps/console/src/screens/Plans.tsx) —
so nothing here is deceptive, only the row's own label omits the channel.
OPERATIONS STILL NEEDS A SHOP RECORD to attach a WhatsApp number to (a branch to register
the sending identity against) — signup itself is unconditional today, so a standalone
buyer already has one before he ever reaches this plan.
STANDALONE_PLANS_ENABLED (operations/app/config.py) is the kill switch: false makes
`may_add` demand الأساس for this row too, same as every other app, without unlisting or
deleting it — existing standalone subscribers are unaffected, only new purchases stop.
NO `credits` KEY YET — the owner wants the price to fund an included usage allowance
(billing-service's own plan-credit-grant mechanism, PLAN_CREDIT_LIMIT_KEY='credits':
a `credits` gauge limit here becomes a wallet credit granted on every paid invoice), but
PRICING_USAGE_HALALAS_PER_1K_TOKENS is still 0 fleet-wide (deploy/services/whatsapp-
assistant.values.yaml) — the real per-token rate was never set, so an included-credits
number would be sized against a cost that is not real yet. Add it once that rate is.
plans.name: بوت خدمة العملاء الذكي

_: جهات الاتصال — THE ONE FREE APP ON THE PRICE LIST, and deliberately so: the owner's own
decision was that registering a customer must be possible «من أي تطبيق», and a shop with
no other product at all must still be able to open the one door that resolves-or-creates a
customer by phone (POST /field/customers/ensure). A price on that door would put the
product's front door behind a paywall nobody else on the price list has to clear first.
amount: 0, ON PURPOSE. billing-service takes the charge at renewal, not at subscribe — see
`_charge_invoice`'s own zero-total branch, which already auto-succeeds a 0-halala invoice
with no gateway call — so a free row needs no special handling there. What DOES need one
is our own `may_subscribe` (services/operations/app/core/subscribe.py), which used to
refuse ANY subscribe with no `payment_token` regardless of price; it now treats a plan
whose resolved price is 0 as paid whether or not a token was sent.
SUBSCRIBED WITH interval='once', NOT 'month' — services/operations/app/api/v1/
subscription.py forces this for every free row, this one included: `once` sets
`period_end` to 0, which the resolver reads as 'never lapses' and the renewal sweep skips
outright, so a free-forever app never re-cycles through a pointless SAR 0 invoice every
month for nothing.
`plan.standalone` — same marker, same reason as «بوت خدمة العملاء الذكي» above: a shop
buying only this holds no base underneath it, so `may_add` must skip its own
base-required rule for THIS row too. `STANDALONE_PLANS_ENABLED` is the same kill switch
for both rows.
`feature.contacts` GRANTS NOTHING BEYOND THE ONE DOOR IT NAMES — it is read by
`subscribed_write_or_customer_creating_app` (services/operations/app/api/subscribed.py)
alongside `feature.base` and `feature.bookings`; it does not touch visits, which stay
behind `feature.visit`/`feature.base` (see «تسجيل زيارة» below) even for a customer this
app just created.
plans.name: جهات الاتصال

_: تسجيل زيارة — THE VISIT REGISTER ITSELF, PULLED OUT FROM UNDER الأساس'S EXCLUSIVE
CONTROL. Until this row, recording a visit was reachable ONLY through `feature.base` — a
shop wanting nothing else from الأساس could not record a single visit without buying the
whole bundle underneath it. This row sells the register on its own, at the same flat 99
every app on this list sells for.
`plan.standalone` — a shop buying only this holds no base underneath it either, same
mechanism as «بوت خدمة العملاء الذكي» and «جهات الاتصال» above.
`feature.base` KEEPS ITS OLD MEANING, UNCHANGED, FOR EXISTING SUBSCRIBERS. This row does
not replace it and does not migrate anybody off it — `subscribed_write_or_visit`
(services/operations/app/api/subscribed.py) accepts EITHER key, so a shop already on
الأساس keeps recording visits exactly as before, with no action needed. Retiring
`feature.base`'s bundling of the visit register in favour of this key everywhere is a
separate, future migration decision — deliberately not made by this row.
plans.name: تسجيل زيارة

_: CAPACITY, NOT AN APP — and the two rows the ladder used to hide. Seats and branches came
bundled with a tier, so a two-branch shop that wanted nothing else had to buy الذكية to
get a second branch.
ONE SEAT PER UNIT, NOT A PACK OF TEN. This row used to grant 10 seats per purchase (named
«10 مقاعد إضافية») on the theory that a repeated purchase was the simpler story to tell an
owner. It was overtaken by the console's own capacity UI (Plans.tsx's CapacityAddonCard,
«السعة» section): a single +/- stepper that moves one subscription's own `quantity` up and
down, never a second row and never a repeated purchase — so the unit this file must grant
IS the unit the stepper adds one of at a time. Left at 10 the stepper's own «1» press
silently bought ten, and the live plan was hand-corrected on the server to grant 1 well
before this file caught up — which is exactly the drift seed-plans.sh exists to close,
and precisely the drift THIS row still carried until now.
THE PRICE IS STILL THE ONLY ONE NOT DERIVED FROM THE OLD LADDER — a starting point, meant
to be argued with; editing this file is the whole mechanism.
plans.name: مقاعد إضافية

_: THE ENTERPRISE SHAPE — priced per conversation, never on the pricing page.
listed=false, so it is invisible to the public list and still subscribable. That is the
whole mechanism: a negotiated customer is moved onto this plan from our panel with an
amount agreed with him, and no code anywhere learns it exists.
IT IS A WHOLE SUBSCRIPTION, NOT AN APP — it carries every key including messages.monthly,
and it is sold INSTEAD of the base rather than beside it. A shop holding both would sum
two message meters into a smaller one, which is why `subscription.activate` refuses it.
The amount here is a PLACEHOLDER, not a price. It is what the plan costs when nobody has
negotiated anything, and the panel overwrites it per subscription.
